newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on institutional selling.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on institutional selling.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down on Friday on institutional selling with market sentiment extremely weak after successive heavy falls in the past few trading days, traders said.
The most actively traded October 1997 contract ended at 21,290 yuan ($2,567) per tonne, losing 410 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 21,700 and hit a low of 21,290.
July fell 400 to 21,100, August 440 to 21,210, September 420 to 21,280, November 410 to 21,390 and December 400 to 21,400.
Combined volume rose sharply to 96,550 tonnes from 45,900.
The contracts opened lower but mostly at their intra-day highs and continued to fall for most of the session with most closing near their intra-day lows.
Traders said institutional sellers built large short positions, triggering panic selling by retail investors.
"Despite the overnight LME gains, institutional selling pushed prices sharply down on pessimism about the short-term trend," one trader said.
"Panic stop loss orders by retail investors then poured into market, resulting in a quick breach of the 21,500-yuan support level," he added.
Physical prices in the Shanghai area fell sharply to the 21,200-21,300 yuan level, from 21,700 from Thursday, due to sharp falls on the futures market, traders said.
Traders said copper prices was likely to continue to fall.

"It is hard to predict what level copper is likely to hit but the outlook is bleak in the short term," a second trader said. "Weak domestic demand for physical copper in the summer season will further hit investor confidence."
Aluminium ended mostly down. July was unchanged at 13,720. August fell 20 to 13,830, September 180 to 13,900 and October 250 to 14,000. Combined volume rose to 2,160 tonnes from 980.
